A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work. Their main text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices are readable and support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v2 reports original neural-network training experiments, including PC–BP gradient comparisons, width/depth sweeps, and learning-regime analyses in Figures 1–4 and the appendix.

after.justification: v3 retains these original experiments and their results, including nonlinear CNN and transformer experiments and the appendix analyses.

M1.justification: The stated transformer computation changes: v2 Eq. 128 includes 1/sqrt(d_i) factors on query, key, and value projections, whereas v3 Eq. 156 omits them while retaining standard-Gaussian initialization. The core PC procedure remains unchanged. The PDFs do not establish whether this specification revision reflects an implementation change or a documentation correction.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same Gaussian-input binary toy task, Fashion-MNIST, CIFAR-10, ImageNet, and character-level Tiny Shakespeare. No dataset, task, or distinct evaluation scenario is added or removed.

E2.justification: BP remains the comparator in the corresponding main-text and appendix experiments. The standard-versus-mean-field parameterisation comparisons are also retained; no evaluated comparison method is added or removed.

E3.justification: The reported transformer loss normalization changes: v2 Eq. 126 encloses cross-entropy within the 1/(2TP) energy factor, whereas v3 Eq. 154 uses a separate 1/P term with sequence-averaged cross-entropy. Other documented budgets, model sizes, metrics, and inference settings remain unchanged. This is a reported normalization revision, without evidence of reruns.

E4.justification: The same width/depth sweeps, feature-learning-parameter sensitivity analyses, standard-parameterisation controls, residual-versus-plain-network comparisons, and Tanh/ReLU experiments remain. The revised discussion of learning regimes introduces no new experimental analysis.

E5.justification: Both versions report three-seed averaging for the gradient-alignment heatmaps, representative runs for Figure 4, and consistency across seeds where error bars are omitted. No repeated-run count or uncertainty-reporting practice changes.

E6.justification: Corresponding experimental figures retain the same plotted data, curves, and comparisons, including all appendix results. No empirical result entries are added, removed, or numerically revised; the nonlinear findings receive more cautious interpretation.

T1.justification: v3 substantially revises Appendices A.4–A.5, including changing PC-specific width corrections from Theta(N^-1/2) to O(N^-1). Desideratum 5 now requires a Theta(1/L) contribution per residual block, and Theorem 2 explicitly assumes L/N tends to zero. New Appendix A.6 derives layerwise and complete-gradient relative-error bounds of O(1/N) for fixed-depth MLPs and O(L/N) for residual networks, with non-vanishing-gradient conditions.

C1.justification: The central PC–BP scaling contribution remains, but v3 adds a quantitative relative-error claim and makes its limiting conditions explicit. The abstract and summary narrow the nonlinear claim from convergence to BP to high gradient alignment, better matching the reported measurements.

C2.justification: Section 3.2 and Appendix A.8.2 newly explain how PC's lazy regime can depart from BP as the output-scaling constant approaches zero. Section 6.2 replaces the suggested factor-L training speedup with a narrower statement about sequential weight-update cost. The main inference-cost, linearity, and short-training limitations remain.

D1.justification: The transformer appendix now explicitly documents token-index inputs, next-token targets, block functions, projection and MLP dimensions, sequence averaging, and omission of the causal mask from notation. Several dimensional expressions are revised. Code access, hardware information, and the experimental recipes are otherwise retained.

R1.justification: v3 adds Yang et al. (2021), Tuning Large Neural Networks via Zero-Shot Hyperparameter Transfer, and uses it for the corresponding attribution. It also describes the relationship to Ishikawa et al.'s SGD parameterisation more cautiously. The overall related-work coverage and positioning remain similar.

P1.justification: The abstract and portions of the introduction, convergence discussion, and limitations are rewritten, with terminology such as 'BP-like' and 'heuristic' refined. A dedicated gradient-convergence appendix section is inserted, while the main narrative and section sequence remain intact.

P2.justification: v3 updates captions and theorem-box layouts and redistributes retained appendix figures across pages. All numbered figures and tables remain; the experimental plots are reused rather than replaced with new displays.

improvement.justification: v2 largely motivated gradient convergence through objective convergence and less accurate derivative scaling. v3's revised derivations and new Appendix A.6 directly address this central justification gap with relative-gradient bounds and explicit conditions. Together with more restrained nonlinear and speedup interpretations, this substantially strengthens the paper's theoretical support. The unexplained connection between revised transformer formulas and retained experiments leaves a limited reproducibility ambiguity.
